about.title: Personal Injury Help in San Gabriel, California
about.longDescription: San Gabriel is a compact, busy city, and its streets carry a steady flow of daily traffic. In the most recent full year on record, San Gabriel saw 155 injury collisions, with 207 people hurt and 2 lives lost. Corridors like San Gabriel Boulevard, Del Mar Avenue, Las Tunas Drive, and Valley Boulevard show up frequently in public crash records simply because they carry so much of the city's traffic between homes, shops, and connecting routes. If you were hurt in a wreck anywhere in San Gabriel, you're not alone, and you don't have to sort through the aftermath by yourself. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can look at what happened and explain your options. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls is hard enough; getting matched with someone who can help shouldn't add to that burden.

whyChoose.title: What San Gabriel Residents Should Know

items.title: You Have Two Years — But the Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth acting sooner rather than later.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation is reduced by your share of fault but not eliminated entirely — even if you were partly responsible for the crash.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so your full experience can be considered.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to Get Legal Help
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency — they only get paid if you recover money, which means you can seek advice without worrying about hourly fees.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in San Gabriel?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your claim involves a government agency, such as a city-owned vehicle, that deadline can be as short as six months. It's best to get guidance early so you don't lose your window.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so being partially responsible doesn't bar you from recovery. Your compensation would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help assess how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in San Gabriel?
items.answer: Public crash records show that collisions are reported most often along San Gabriel Boulevard, Del Mar Avenue, Las Tunas Drive, and Valley Boulevard, which are among the city's busiest corridors. Reported crashes also tend to peak on Fridays between 6 and 8 p.m. These are simply neutral counts reflecting traffic volume, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency. That means there's no fee unless they recover money on your behalf.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is not a law firm and does not provide legal representation. We simply help connect injured people in San Gabriel with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate their situation.
